scenes.say: What’s the single most important thing to remember when building accessible web apps?

scenes.label: POUR
scenes.say: WCAG is built on four principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust. We call them POUR.
Always use semantic HTML elements first. ARIA is for when HTML can’t provide the meaning you need.
Test your site with just a keyboard. Can you reach and use every interactive element in order?

scenes.title: Screen Reader Check
scenes.say: Screen readers rely on your markup. If you use the right elements, they’ll announce content correctly.

scenes.question: Should you add ARIA everywhere?
scenes.right: No. Use semantic HTML first. Only add ARIA if needed.
scenes.say: Here’s a common interview trap: Should you add ARIA everywhere? No. Semantic HTML is best. Only use ARIA if HTML can’t do the job.
